description.narrative:
1. The Government of Zimbabwe through the Ministries of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Resettlement; Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Enterprises Development, and tripartite partners, have developed and implemented tools to improve productivity and business continuity, value chain development and decent work for small scale green agro-entrepreneurs.
2. The findings of an assessment of agribusinesses in the context of COVID-19 pandemic provided guidance to the tripartite constituents and private sector players in the sector to address decent work challenges and low productivity of agribusinesses. Involvement of the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community and Small and Medium Enterprises Development resulted in advocacy and raising awareness of addressing gender-related barriers for decent work as means of enhancing women economic empowerment, as women especially in the rural economy were the most affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.
3. Two on-line action checklists have provided practical guidance to agro-entrepreneurs, especially youth and women-led enterprises, to improve occupational safety and health (OSH) and COVID-19-related safety measures, productivity, decent work and green business development practices. Through the capacity building training and engagement, various government departments have adopted the action checklists as part of their capacity building efforts to enhance technical and business skills required to promote decent work in the agriculture sector. The rollout of the action checklist was supported by the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU), Employers Confederation of Zimbabwe (EMCOZ) and the above-mentioned Government Departments. The ILO developed the methodology for measuring the key rural economy dimensions, provided technical guidance for the assessment, and trained key stakeholders (25 government officials and other intermediary organizations received training to use the tools to address safety, productivity, green jobs and decent work deficits among both intermediaries and SMEs).
An enterprise-based assessment of the rural economy was produced in August 2021 to inform the development of an Action Plan that addresses the decent work challenges and the root causes of underperformance and low productivity of agro-business in the context of COVID-19 in Zimbabwe. The assessment report was validated in a workshop with tripartite constituents and other key stakeholders. The work has enhanced the capacity of policy makers to make informed policy decisions.
In October 2021, the ILO produced two Action Checklists, informed by the enterprise-based assessment of the rural economy, to help address OSH challenges, including COVID-19, productivity and decent work deficits in small and medium enterprises in the agriculture sector. Capacity building through a two-day training course was conducted for 25 Government officers and other intermediary organizations as means to operationalize the checklist.
In October 2021, ILO developed and published four digital stories of most significant change, with a focus on innovation and green business development service diversification to showcase emerging good practices in business continuity, productivity enhancement and value chain development.
The Government of Sweden supported ILO's action in this area.
